chunks: 914 – And among what al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in al-ʿIlal, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, is that he said:

"The people were only commanded to the adhan for many reasons. Among them is that it be a reminder for the forgetful, an alert for the heedless, and an informing for one who is ignorant of the time and has been occupied away from it. And so that the mu'adhdhin thereby may be one calling to the worship of the Creator, encouraging toward it, affirming His tawhid, proclaiming faith openly, declaring Islam openly, and announcing it for the one who forgets it. He is only called a mu'adhdhin because he announces by the adhan the salat. It only begins with takbir and ends with tahlil because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed that the beginning be with His remembrance and His Name, and the Name of Allah is in the takbir at the start of the phrase and in the tahlil at its end. It was only made in pairs, pair by pair, so that it may be a repetition in the ears of the listeners, confirming it for them: if someone is inattentive to the first, he will not be inattentive to the second. And because the salat is two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, therefore the adhan was made pair by pair. And the takbir at the beginning of the adhan was made four times because the beginning of the adhan starts suddenly, and there is no speech before it to alert the listener to it; so the first two were made as an alert for the listeners to what comes after them in the adhan."

And after the takbir, the two testimonies were placed, because the first of faith is tawhid and acknowledging to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, His Oneness; and the second is acknowledging the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله by the رسالة, and that obeying them both and knowing them both are joined together. And because the foundation of faith is only the two testimonies, they were made as two testimonies, two testimonies, just as in all other rights there are two witnesses. So when the servant acknowledges to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His Oneness, and acknowledges to the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله the رسالة, then he has acknowledged the totality of faith, because the foundation of faith is only in Allah and in His Messenger. And after the two testimonies, the call to salat was placed, because the adhan was only instituted for the place of salat, and it is only a call to salat in the middle of the adhan, and a call to success and to the best of deeds. And the closing of the speech was made with His Name just as it was opened with His Name."

key_terms.خَيْرِ ٱلْعَمَلِ: the best of deeds, mentioned as part of the call within the adhan
key_terms.ٱلتَّكْبِيرِ: the saying of 'Allahu Akbar' at the opening of the adhan
key_terms.ٱلتَّهْلِيلِ: the declaration 'Lā ilāha illā Allāh' with which the adhan concludes
key_terms.ٱلشَّهَادَتَانِ: the two testimonies forming the foundation of faith
key_terms.ٱلْأَذَانِ: the call to prayer that announces the time and summons people to salat
key_terms.ٱلْفَلَاحِ: success to which the adhan calls the listeners
key_terms.ٱلْمُؤَذِّنُ: the one who proclaims the adhan and calls people to worship

ai.seo_question: Why was the adhan instituted and why are its phrases arranged in this order?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the wisdoms behind the adhan, describing it as a reminder, an alert, and a public proclamation of tawhid, faith, and Islam. It also explains the order and repetition of its phrases, showing how its structure reflects both theological foundations and the function of calling people to salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.914 – Imam al-Ridha (as) was reported to have said as mentioned by al-Fadl ibn Shadhan (may Allah (swt) have mercy on him):

"People were commanded to perform the adhan (call to prayer) for many reasons. Among them is that it serves as a reminder for those who forget, an awakening for the heedless, a means of informing those who are unaware of the prayer time due to being preoccupied, and it makes the mu'adhdhin (caller) a proclaimer of worship to the Creator, encouraging others to it, affirming His Oneness, proclaiming faith, and making Islam known to those who might forget. He is called the 'mu'adhdhin' because he announces the call to prayer.
The adhan begins with 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah (swt) is the Greatest) and concludes with 'La ilaha illAllah (swt)' (There is no god but Allah (swt)) because Allah (swt), the Exalted, willed that His Name be mentioned at the beginning and the end. It is repeated in pairs (two-by-two) to ensure that it is heard clearly and emphasized; if one statement is missed, the second will be heard. Furthermore, since the prayer itself is performed in units of two rak'ahs, the adhan was also structured similarly.
The initial four takbirs (saying 'Allahu Akbar') serve to alert the listener since it begins abruptly and there is no preceding word to capture attention.

Following the takbirs are the two testimonies of faith, as the essence of belief starts with the declaration of Allah’s (swt) Oneness and the acknowledgment of the Prophethood of Muhammad (sw). These two testimonies are linked because faith is rooted in both recognizing Allah (swt) and His Messenger, and just as other legal matters require two witnesses, so does faith in its complete form.
The call to prayer is then followed by an invitation to salah (prayer), which is the purpose of the adhan, and a call to success and the best of deeds. Finally, it concludes with the mention of Allah’s (swt) Name, just as it began with His Name."
